# S49 — Fall back to the next matrix row on a rate limit or error

Owner 2026-10-20: when Codex is rate-limited or fails, the engine should fall back to the Claude row (matrix: Sol high then Sonnet medium). By hand, relay-call.sh falls back on a rate limit and the orchestrator picks the next row on an implementer error; the engine must do both. Depends on the Codex adapter.

## Why

Owner 2026-10-20: when Codex is rate-limited or fails, the engine should fall back to the Claude row (matrix: Sol high then Sonnet medium). By hand, relay-call.sh falls back on a rate limit and the orchestrator picks the next row on an implementer error; the engine must do both. Depends on the Codex adapter.

- `internal/engine` (lineup, retry), `internal/daemon`, tests, `docs/design.md`.

## Failing tests

- TestRateLimitFallsBackToTheNextRow: the first row's round exits rate_limited; a new role record starts on the second row in the same state; the run keeps both records.
- TestAnErrorExitStillStopsTheSlice: an error exit stops the slice with the reason (the existing TestAnExitNotClassifiedOkStopsTheSliceWithTheReason, internal/engine/stop_test.go:14, stays as it is; decision 114).
- TestFallbackIsSticky: after a fallback, the same role's next round starts on the fallback row, with no new run.json field (decision 115).
- TestResumeOnlyWithTheSameVendorAndModel: latestSession (internal/engine/round.go:44) skips a session from another vendor or model.
- TestRateLimitOnTheLastRowStopsWithTheReasons: the slice stops, and Reason names the exit of each row.
- TestRunPlanKeepsEveryRowWithAnAdapter: the plan keeps the lineup list in order (internal/daemon/runs.go:224-231).

## Implement

1. Write the failing tests first in internal/engine/fallback_test.go (new). Extend fakeRunner (internal/engine/harness_test.go:70-91) so a test can make a given row exit ExitRateLimited.
2. Add a helper in internal/engine/engine.go next to lineup (engine.go:141-148): currentEntry(rec, role) returns the index into rec.Lineup[role]. It matches the role's last RoleRecord (Vendor, Model, Effort). If that record's Exit is "rate_limited", it returns the next index. No new run.json field (decision 115).
3. internal/engine/round.go:144: replace `entry, _ := lineup(rec.Lineup, r.role)` with currentEntry. If no row is left, stop with the reason (step 6).
4. internal/engine/round.go:44-52 latestSession: take the entry's Vendor and Model, and skip any role record that differs (decision 114 rule, via the resume rule in design.md:392-396). Call site: round.go:176.
5. round.go:250 already saves role.Exit, so the next call sees the rate-limited record.
6. round.go:264-270: before the stop switch, if class is ExitRateLimited and a next row exists, end the ledger step as fail and return with the state unchanged. advance (engine.go:225-257) then runs the state again on the next row. If no row is left, fall through to the existing stop.
7. The attempt counter in runRound counts the same role and round, so a fallback row writes a "-attempt-2" report name (existing behaviour; check it in a test).
8. internal/daemon/runs.go:224-231: keep all rows with an adapter, in lineup order (claude-only works now; codex rows need S47).
9. Check the mapping: internal/daemon/runner.go:35-36 maps claude.ClassRateLimited to engine.ExitRateLimited, and engine/runner.go:29 defines it.
10. docs/design.md:392-396: add the stickiness rule (decision 115) and the same-vendor resume rule.
11. No TUI or golden change expected. If the pane shows a row's vendor, check the goldens.
